entries.claim: The 16-byte allocation does NOT come from sub_003437F3 - it takes sub_001F7E00's early exit into sub_001F7E57, which allocates through the MANAGER's own vtable+0xCC. So the manager's pool allocator returned the pool's own base address, 0x011CE000, and the constructor then overwrote the pool header and first array slot
entries.evidence: Followed the allocation to its source. sub_001F7E00 reads size from esp+4 and a PREFIX size from esp+0x10 into edi, computes esi = size + edi, and then has THREE outcomes: two early exits to sub_001F7E57 (when the esp+0x14 argument is non-zero, and when an ICALL through MEM32(0x5BC5DC)'s vtable+0x58 returns non-zero), and only as a fallback does it call sub_003437F3. sub_001F7E57 is five lines: `edx = MEM32(eax); PUSH esi; ecx = eax; ICALL MEM32(edx + 0xCC);` then `eax = eax + edi` - allocate size+prefix through an allocator OBJECT's vtable+0xCC, then bias the result past the prefix. That is a standard allocate-with-header idiom, and vtable+0xCC on vtbl 0x003F4770 is sub_001EC5E0, the manager's allocate thunk identified in ledger #38. THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE that this is the path taken: sub_003437F3 carries PERMANENT instrumentation (a manual addition recording every returned pointer into g_alloc_trace, deliberately not marked /* PROBE */ so strip_probes leaves it), and its crash-time dump reads "Allocator returned 10 pointer(s)" listing 0x01082000, 0x01083000, 0x01085000, 0x01086000, 0x01087000, 0x01088A90, 0x01089A90, 0x011CD000, 0x011CE000, 0x01311000 - and explicitly "0 failed (returned NULL), 0 repeated a live address". So sub_003437F3 handed out 0x011CE000 EXACTLY ONCE and never repeated any address. The duplicate therefore cannot have come from it. Since sub_00222628's 16-byte request demonstrably returned 0x011CE000 (#67) and that value appears only once in the trace, the request must have gone down the untraced sub_001F7E57 path. CONCLUSION: the MANAGER'S OWN POOL ALLOCATOR returned the pool's base address. 0x011CE000 is MEM32(manager + 0x70) - the pool - with its control word at +0 and its deferred-free array at +4. Asked for 16 bytes, it handed back a block starting AT the pool base rather than at a carved block inside it, so the constructor's vtable store landed on the control word and its refcount on array slot 0. That is why no free marker was ever written (#66): nothing was freed. The pool allocator simply carved from the wrong offset. NOT YET CONFIRMED and worth one probe before acting: that vtable+0xCC on THIS object is sub_001EC5E0 (it is on vtbl 0x003F4770 per #38, but the allocator object here comes from MEM32(eax) at sub_001F7E57's entry and has not been identified for this call), and what edi (the prefix size) is - if edi is 0 the returned pointer is the raw block base, which would explain landing exactly on the pool base rather than a few bytes in. Probe sub_001F7E57's entry for eax, MEM32(eax), MEM32(MEM32(eax)+0xCC), esi and edi. Tree clean: probes stripped, 82/2/22/8 deterministic, reached 55.

entries.claim: ROOT CAUSE of the sub_00205170 crash: the pool allocator sub_001EC5E0 returns NULL (a legitimate failure) but CLOBBERS callee-saved edi, leaving 0x011CE000 in it. sub_001F7E57's `eax = eax + edi` prefix bias then turns the NULL into 0x011CE000 - the pool's own base - so the caller's null check passes and the constructor overwrites the pool header. Callee-saved-clobber class, same as sub_001FAB40 losing esi (#52)
entries.evidence: MEASURED, two probe lines, deterministic build (82 kernel calls / 2 failed icalls / 22 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, reached 55). Probes on both ends of sub_001F7E57, the untraced allocation path identified in #68: "[A:ENT] obj=0x01088A90 vtbl=0x003F4770 target=0x001EC5E0 size=0x00000010 edi=0x00000000" and "[A:RET] raw=0x00000000 edi=0x011CE000 -> 0x011CE000". Exactly one allocation takes this path all boot. THREE facts, each read directly: (1) The ICALL target IS sub_001EC5E0 on vtbl 0x003F4770, confirming ledger #38's identification for this call site - that was an assumption in #68 and is now measured. (2) The allocator RETURNED NULL. raw eax = 0x00000000. Asking the pool for 16 bytes FAILED. That failure is honest and sub_00222628 is written to handle it - it does `if (TEST_Z(eax, eax))` immediately on return (#67). (3) edi entered sub_001F7E57 as 0x00000000 and left the ICALL as 0x011CE000. edi is CALLEE-SAVED on x86, so sub_001EC5E0 is required to restore it; because the registers are C globals in the lifted tree, a callee that fails to restore one silently rewrites its caller's value. THE MECHANISM, end to end: sub_001F7E00 computes esi = size + prefix and puts the prefix in edi (here prefix = 0, so edi = 0). It tail-jumps to sub_001F7E57, which allocates size+prefix through the object's vtable+0xCC and then biases the result past the prefix with `eax = eax + edi`. With edi correctly preserved at 0 the arithmetic is 0 + 0 = 0, sub_00222628's null check fires, and the boot takes the allocation-failure path - faithful behaviour. With edi clobbered to 0x011CE000 the arithmetic is 0 + 0x011CE000 = 0x011CE000, the null check PASSES, and sub_00222628 hands that address to the constructor as `this`. sub_001F7CD0 then writes vtable 0x3EEAE8 to MEM32(this) and refcount 1 to MEM32(this + 4). But 0x011CE000 is MEM32(manager + 0x70) - the live pool - whose control word is at +0 and whose deferred-free array starts at +4. So the vtable store lands on the pool control word and the refcount 1 lands on array slot 0. That is the 1 at 0x011CE004 the trace-watch caught (#65), and it is why no free marker was ever written (#66): nothing was freed, and nothing was allocated either. sub_00205170 then reads the array, takes esi = 1, and either walks to MEM32(edi + 1) at +0x682 or reads the footer MEM32(1 - 4) = MEM32(0xFFFFFFFD) at +0x6F3 - the two faces of one bug (#62), which is why the site flips on layout changes. This closes the chain from the crash back to a single lifter defect. NEXT STEP: find where inside sub_001EC5E0 (or one of its callees) edi is lost, and fix the preservation - not the arithmetic in sub_001F7E57, which is a faithful lift. Run faithful on sub_001EC5E0 first; #46 showed the loss is more often in a callee than in the named function. SEPARATE QUESTION, do not conflate: WHY the pool allocator fails to serve 16 bytes at all. Fixing edi makes the boot take the honest failure path, which may surface as a clean out-of-memory rather than progress - the same shape as #40. Both want fixing; the clobber first, because it is corrupting memory.

entries.claim: The edi clobber of #69 IS the 40-byte stack leak of #39 - one and the same defect. This RETRACTS #40's decision not to fix it: the leak does not merely strand stack inside a fatal OOM reporter, it makes every caller's POP restore callee-saved registers from the wrong slot, and that is what corrupts the pool and causes the current crash. Fixing the 40 bytes is the fix for the wall
entries.evidence: MEASURED by walking edi and g_esp together down the allocator chain with entry + every-return-site probes (31 points across sub_001EC5E0, sub_00211530, sub_0020F860, sub_0020EFD0, sub_0020F209, sub_0020F0B2), each site with its OWN counter. THE CONTROL, from the same run - a healthy sub_0020F860 call: "IN edi=0x00000010 esp=0x00F7FE90" and "R3 edi=0x00000010 esp=0x00F7FE90". esp restored exactly, edi preserved exactly. That is what a correct call looks like, and most calls in the log do this. THE FAILING CALL, the one feeding sub_001F7E57: "IN edi=0x00000010 esp=0x00F7FEAC" then "R4 edi=0x011CE000 esp=0x00F7FE84". 0x00F7FEAC - 0x00F7FE84 = 0x28 = 40 BYTES, and edi comes back as the pool pointer. THE SAME 40 BYTES RIDES ALL THE WAY OUT, every level inheriting it: sub_00211530 IN 0x00F7FEEC -> R5 0x00F7FEC4 (-0x28, edi=0x011CE000); sub_001EC5E0 IN 0x00F7FEFC -> R0 0x00F7FED4 (-0x28, edi=0x011CE000). sub_001EC5E0 then returns to sub_001F7E57, where `eax = eax + edi` adds that 0x011CE000 to a NULL allocation. WHERE THE 40 GOES, unchanged from #39: sub_0020F860 IN 0x00F7FEAC -> sub_0020EFD0 IN 0x00F7FE74 -> sub_0020EFD0 R0 (its tail-jump) 0x00F7FE34, a 0x40 drop that exactly matches the 64-byte frame sub_0020EFD0 allocates, so that function is CORRECT -> sub_0020F209 IN 0x00F7FE34 -> sub_0020F209 R7 (the full epilogue) 0x00F7FE4C. R7 unwound only 0x18 of the 0x40 it owes; 0x00F7FE74 was due, so it is short by exactly 0x28. And the register proves the pops read the wrong slots: edi at R7 is 0x00F7FE1C, a STACK ADDRESS, not any plausible saved value. sub_0020F860's own epilogue then pops ITS edi from a slot 40 bytes off and gets 0x011CE000. This is precisely #38's finding ("the stack is 40 bytes too deep at its epilogue, so POP32 reads uninitialised stack instead of the saved esi") reproduced on edi, one caller further out. WHY THIS RETRACTS #40: #40 refused the fix on the grounds that the leak lives inside the game's fatal out-of-memory reporter, which ends in `goto self` by design, so "repairing it buys a clean hang, not progress". The first half is right and the second half is wrong. The reporter path IS being taken - the pool allocator genuinely fails to serve 16 bytes and returns NULL - but the path RETURNS rather than hanging (R7, the balanced epilogue, is reached), and on the way out it destroys the callee-saved registers of four stacked callers. The damage is not confined to the reporter. It is what converts an honest allocation failure into a write through the pool's own base address, and thence to the sub_00205170 crash. So the leak must be fixed, and #40's "not worth fixing" no longer holds. NEXT STEP, unchanged from #39's open question and now worth doing: account for every push against every cleanup on sub_0020F209's path to its third sub_0020F0B2 tail-jump and find which 40 bytes are pushed without cleanup. The likely shape is arguments pushed for the two sub_001E8F30 calls or the vtable+0x54 ICALL whose cdecl cleanup (`esp + 8`, `esp + 0xC`, `esp + 0x14`) sits on a branch the retry path skips. SECOND, SEPARATE BUG still open and NOT to be conflated: why the pool allocator refuses a 16-byte request at all. Fixing the leak alone makes the boot take the honest failure branch in sub_00222628, which may read as a clean out-of-memory rather than as progress. Tree clean: 96 probe lines stripped, build verified.

entries.claim: `reached` counts ONLY indirect dispatch - RECOMP_ICALL, RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE and RECOMP_ITAIL are the only three callers of recomp_mark_reached(). Direct RECOMP_ABI_CALL sites are plain C calls and are never counted, so `reached` is structurally blind to directly-called code and CAN fall while the boot runs strictly more. Added g_callsite_count to cover the blind spot
entries.evidence: Settled by reading the implementation, not by inference from run numbers. recomp_mark_reached() is defined at recomp_types.h:252 and grep finds exactly THREE call sites, all indirect: RECOMP_ICALL (line ~597), RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE (~634) and RECOMP_ITAIL (~649), each as `if (_fn) { recomp_mark_reached(_va); _fn(); }`. RECOMP_ABI_CALL - the direct-call macro, 1624+ sites in recomp_0015.c alone - expanded to bare `fn()` with no marking at all. So g_reached_count is "distinct INDIRECT targets", never "distinct functions entered". THE HEADER ITSELF ADMITS THIS at recomp_types.h:233: "It counts indirect-call targets, not every function - direct calls are ordinary C calls with nothing to hook. In this engine that is a good proxy: 18,556 generated call sites are indirect, because the whole thing is virtual dispatch through igMetaObject." The proxy argument is sound in general and fails in one specific case: a fix that REMOVES indirect work. That is exactly what #72 did - seeding the two stubs cut a vtable-heavy retry spin out of the allocator, so the boot stopped re-resolving the same slots and ran straight-line code instead. Judged on `reached` alone it read as a regression while kernel_calls went 82 -> 330 and the backtrace 4 -> 18 frames. This retroactively explains #72's conflict and means `reached` should NOT be treated as the sole gate; it is one of two numbers. THE FIX, purely additive and semantically inert: RECOMP_MARK_SITE() in recomp_types.h, one `static uint8_t` per textual call site set on first execution, invoked from BOTH arms of RECOMP_ABI_CALL (the plain one and the RECOMP_CHECK_ABI one). g_callsite_count is defined in recomp_manual.c and printed by recomp_coverage_dump() alongside the existing line. Cost is one predictable branch and one byte of .bss per site; it cannot alter behaviour because it touches no register, no memory model and no control flow. It counts call SITES rather than functions deliberately - finer grained, and marking function entries would mean editing all 30,002 generated bodies instead of one macro. FIRST READING on the current post-seed tree: "distinct=42 of 1032192 dispatch targets reached" and "callsites=177 distinct direct call sites executed", build deterministic at 330/3/28/8. The pre-seed comparison is being measured now by rebuilding recomp_seed.c from a seed list with the two addresses removed (`--from-list ... --apply`, the tool's supported path), with seed_list.json backed up to seed_list.json.bak_settle first. SEPARATE FINDING worth its own work, spotted while reading the header: RECOMP_CHECK_ABI is an EXISTING build mode that validates ebx/esi/edi across every direct call and flags esp leaving the stack range, naming the callee - `recomp_abi_violation()` and `recomp_esp_escape()`. That is an automated detector for the exact bug class (#38, #52, #69, #71) this project has been finding by hand, one probe pair at a time. Nobody appears to have run it. Try a RECOMP_CHECK_ABI build.

entries.claim: THE POOL REFUSES 16 BYTES BECAUSE OUR OWN KERNEL BRIDGE IGNORES THE REQUESTED BASE ADDRESS. bridge_NtAllocateVirtualMemory reads base_hint then calls xbox_HeapAlloc(size, 4096) for MEM_RESERVE, returning the bump pointer instead of the requested base. The engine reserves at an address it verified free, gets a different one back, checks `if (returned != requested) fail`, and gives up. Measured off by exactly 0x3000 twice
entries.evidence: Walked the whole chain top to bottom on the CURRENT build (330/3/28/8 deterministic), re-measuring rather than trusting #40/#41 because fix #44 and the #72 seeds both changed the code underneath them. STEP 1 - sub_001F09D0: ten loop iterations, every one ending edi = -1. Probes at all ten labels show CMIT/STAT/UNDO/STA2/WIN/FAIL never fire, so the commit/undo logic #41 analysed is NEVER REACHED on this build. That supersedes #41's picture without contradicting its measurements - the code changed. STEP 2 - the allocator gate: vtable+0x70 is sub_001FE850, whose entire test is `ecx = MEM32(0x46A668) >> 0x1A; edx = MEM32(0x5BBAD0) >> 0x1A; if (ecx <= edx) ok; else return -1`. At identity values MIN=0xFFFFFFFF MAX=0 that is 63 <= 0, false, so it refuses. STEP 3 - the bootstrap: the ONLY writer of MIN and MAX is sub_001FE670's tail (recomp_0015.c:5136-5146, a min/max extender), and its ONLY caller is loc_001F0B03, which is downstream of a SUCCESSFUL allocation. Circular by construction, so something must break the cycle - and that is the fallback at loc_001F09FB. Probed it: "[Q:A4PRE] vtbl=0x003EECB0 target=0x001FFD50" on all 10 calls, "[Q:A4POST] ret=0xFFFFFFFF" on all 10. STEP 4 - walked all 65 labels of sub_001FFDA1, the OS reservation logic (sub_0034D457 queries, sub_0034D3ED reserves/commits, sub_0034D41B releases). The scan WORKS: it walks ebx 0x00000000 -> 0x00010000 -> 0x00780000 -> 0x00F80000 -> 0x0108CA90, testing `mbi.State == 0x10000 (MEM_FREE) && mbi.RegionSize >= edi` at loc_001FFEB0/loc_001FFEBE, and it FINDS a free region of 0x02F70000 - so ledger #35's MEM_FREE work is delivering correctly. It then aligns to base 0x01090000 and reserves 0x140000 bytes with flags 0x2000 (MEM_RESERVE) via sub_0034D3ED at loc_001FFF2D. THE FAILURE, at loc_001FFF3B: eax = 0x0108D000. The call returned a DIFFERENT address than the 0x01090000 requested. loc_001FFF86 loads ecx = the requested base and loc_001FFF8E does `if (eax != ecx) goto loc_0020012B` - the failure exit, which returns MEM32(esp+0x14), seeded to 0xFFFFFFFF by sub_001FFD50. Second attempt identical: requested 0x011D0000, got 0x011CD000. BOTH OFF BY EXACTLY 0x3000. STEP 5 - confirmed in our own source. kernel_bridge.c:388 bridge_NtAllocateVirtualMemory reads `base_hint = BRIDGE_MEM32(base_ptr)` at line 399 and even LOGS it at 402, handles the MEM_COMMIT-without-RESERVE case at 422, and then at line 435 does `uint32_t xbox_va = xbox_HeapAlloc(size, 4096);` - base_hint is simply DISCARDED for MEM_RESERVE. xbox_memory_layout.c:659 xbox_HeapAlloc is a pure bump allocator with no address parameter at all: `result = (g_heap_next + alignment - 1) & ~(alignment - 1)`. So a reservation at a caller-chosen address is impossible to express. THIS IS A PORT BUG IN OUR KERNEL, NOT A LIFTER BUG AND NOT GAME BEHAVIOUR. The engine is doing the correct and normal thing: query for a free region, reserve exactly there, verify it got what it asked for. PROPOSED FIX: honour base_hint for MEM_RESERVE. Add an xbox_HeapAllocAt(base, size) that, when base >= xbox_HeapHighWater() and base + size <= XBOX_HEAP_BASE + XBOX_HEAP_SIZE, sets g_heap_next = base + size, zero-fills, and returns base exactly. That is consistent with what bridge_NtQueryVirtualMemory already reports since #35 - everything from the high-water mark up is MEM_FREE - so any base the engine picks from a MEM_FREE report is by construction above the bump pointer and safe to hand over. Both observed requests (0x01090000 vs bump 0x0108D000, and 0x011D0000 vs 0x011CD000) are ABOVE the bump pointer, so the simple forward-skip covers the measured cases. Fall back to the current behaviour when base_hint is 0. EXPECT ON FIX: the reservation succeeds, sub_001FFDA1 returns a real address, sub_001F09D0 reaches loc_001F0A96 and then loc_001F0B03, sub_001FE670 registers the region, MIN/MAX get real values, and sub_001FE850 stops refusing - which should also revive sub_001FE670, sub_001ECAD0, sub_001F83D0 and sub_001F8408, the functions #74 recorded as going dormant. Measure with tools_data/diff_reached.py against baseline_reached_postseed.txt, not on counts alone. Tree clean: 233 probe lines stripped.

entries.evidence: Followed #77's lead a second time: this run's failed icalls were 0x00000001, 0x00000000 and 0x00216F70; sub_00216F70 did not exist in the tree and dry-ran to a clean 6-byte extent. Seeded (seed_list.json now 1164). RESULT, deterministic 2 of 2: reached 99 -> 101, callsites 382 -> 357, heap_allocs 25 -> 23, failed_icalls 3 -> 5, kernel_calls unchanged at 44. Set diff: 4 gained (sub_001EB200, sub_001EB250, sub_00216F70, sub_00217FD0), 2 lost (sub_0022E0C0, sub_00233490) - and the two lost are NOT the abandoned-failure-path pattern that justified #76's losses, they are from the band #77 had just won. WHY IT IS KEPT ANYWAY: I checked the lifted body rather than trusting the extent, because a 6-byte auto-detected function is exactly the shape of a truncated fragment and the 2026-08-05 regression came from unverified fragments. recomp_seed.c:119077 reads in full `void sub_00216F70(void) { loc_00216F70: eax = MEM32(0x5BC274); esp += 4; return; /* ret */ }` - two instructions, `mov eax, [0x5BC274]` then `ret`, exactly 6 bytes, a COMPLETE getter returning the same global singleton sub_00221F50 reads. It is not truncated. A faithful lift that changes downstream behaviour is REVEALING a bug elsewhere, not causing one: previously the ICALL failed and RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE handed back eax = 0, so the engine was branching on a fake null. Reverting correct code to keep a nicer number would be the wrong trade. The callsites drop is recorded as an open question, not explained away. THE LEAD IS NOW EXHAUSTED: this run's failed icall targets are 0x00000001, 0x00000000, 0x00000010, 0xFFFFFFFF and 0x0000000B - all garbage pointers, no plausible code addresses left, so the cheap #77 method has no more candidates at this wall. THE SYSTEMIC FINDING, which is the real value of this step: esp is ABOVE the top of the stack in BOTH recent crashes. The stack region is 0x00780000-0x00F80000 and grows DOWN, so a valid esp is always below 0x00F80000. Measured esp = 0x00F80120 at sub_0022C2A0 + 0x279, and esp = 0x00F8031C at sub_00204800 + 0x24D - past the top by 0x120 and 0x31C, and getting worse. That is an UNDERFLOW (too many pops), the opposite direction from the 40-byte leak of #70/#71. NOTE triage labels these "heap" because 0x00F80000 is XBOX_HEAP_BASE, which is misleading - it is the stack having run off its top, not a heap pointer. THE TOOL FOR THIS ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NEVER BEEN RUN: recomp_types.h defines RECOMP_CHECK_ABI, which wraps every direct call to verify ebx/esi/edi are restored (recomp_abi_violation) and to flag esp leaving RECOMP_ESP_LO 0x00700000 .. RECOMP_ESP_HI 0x00F80000, NAMING THE CALLEE (recomp_esp_escape). CMakeLists.txt:28 exposes it as an option. Configured and building now via `cmake -S . -B build_abi -DRECOMP_CHECK_ABI=ON` in a SEPARATE directory so the normal build is untouched. This is an automated detector for the exact bug class that has dominated 2026-08-07 - #38, #52, #69, #71 were all found by hand, one probe pair at a time. CURRENT WALL: write at Xbox VA 0xFFFFFF03 in sub_00204800 + 0x24D (recomp_0015.c ~17954), esi = -1, eax = 0xFFFFFF00, ebx = 0x65637275 which is ASCII "urce" so string data is in a register. Backtrace sub_001A1C97 -> sub_0019F22E -> sub_0019F196 -> sub_001A1C23 -> sub_00011E40 -> sub_00239E50 -> sub_002392E0 -> sub_002155B0 -> sub_0020DA95 -> sub_0020A360 -> sub_00204800.

entries.claim: RECOMP_CHECK_ABI now runs and works - 23 distinct callee-save violations captured to tools_data/abi_violations.txt. But it did NOT fire on esp, which is the important NEGATIVE result: the stack underflow does not happen across any DIRECT call, so it must be an ICALL or a tail-jump chain. The violation list needs triage, not blind trust - several are string-copy code where esi/edi are legitimately consumed
entries.evidence: FIRST EVER RUN of RECOMP_CHECK_ABI on this project - the mode has existed in recomp_types.h and CMakeLists.txt:28 the whole time and nobody had used it. Built into a SEPARATE directory so the normal build is untouched: `cmake -S . -B build_abi -DRECOMP_CHECK_ABI=ON` then `cmake --build build_abi --config Release`, clean apart from four pre-existing C4700 uninitialised-local warnings in recomp_0017.c (mm2, mm3, ebp x2 - worth a separate look). VALIDITY CHECK FIRST: the instrumented binary reports "distinct=101" and "callsites=357", identical to the normal build, and crashes the same way (0xC0000005). So the checking is behaviour-neutral and its observations describe the real run, not a perturbed one. RESULT 1 - 23 distinct callee-save violations, saved to tools_data/abi_violations.txt. Format is "[ABI] sub_X did not restore:  ebx BEFORE->AFTER  esi ...  edi ...". Examples: sub_003432E3 loses all three; sub_00204020 loses esi and edi; sub_0021ACD0 loses all three; sub_002235D0, sub_00209650, sub_001EA600, sub_002096B0, sub_0020E520, sub_002226E0, sub_001EA730, sub_001EA770, sub_002041D0, sub_001EA6B0, sub_00227F90, sub_00236500, sub_00342AA0, sub_001183A0 and a run of sub_00023440/70/80/4C0/4E0/500. DO NOT TREAT THIS AS A BUG LIST - IT NEEDS TRIAGE. Several entries show ASCII in the "after" values: 0x6769203A = ": ig", 0x624F6174 = "taOb", 0x654D6769 = "igMe", 0x65726854 = "Thre", 0x45747865 = "extE", 0x0163656A = "jec". Those are string bytes being moved, i.e. rep movsd / rep stosd style copies where esi and edi are the source and destination pointers and are legitimately consumed. A function whose whole job is a memory copy will trip this check without being wrong. The sub_00023440-sub_00023500 cluster all showing the identical "edi 0044B0A4->00000001" also smells like one CRT-ish helper family rather than six independent bugs. Triage by asking whether the caller actually depends on the register afterwards - that is what made #37/#38/#52/#69 real. RESULT 2, AND THE MORE USEFUL ONE - A NEGATIVE: recomp_esp_escape NEVER FIRED. Zero esp reports in the whole run. The check is `if ((g_esp < 0x00700000 || g_esp > 0x00F80000) && (esp_before >= 0x00700000 && esp_before <= 0x00F80000)) recomp_esp_escape(...)`, so it catches the TRANSITION out of range across a direct call. The crash has esp = 0x00F8031C, which IS out of range (initial esp is 0x00F7FFF0 per the startup banner "Stack: 8192 KB at Xbox VA 0x00780000 (ESP = 0x00F7FFF0)", so the stack has been popped 0x32C bytes more than pushed). Since no direct call was observed carrying esp out of range, THE OVER-POP IS NOT IN A DIRECT CALL. That leaves: an ICALL (RECOMP_ICALL / RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE / RECOMP_ITAIL are NOT wrapped by RECOMP_ABI_CALL and so are unchecked), a tail-jump fragment chain, or arithmetic inside one function. This rules out a large search space for one build. NEXT STEP, and it is cheap: extend the esp range check into RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE and RECOMP_ITAIL, where the target address is already in hand and can be printed - that would name the over-popping indirect callee the same way recomp_esp_escape names a direct one. Given #71 found TWO generic `g_esp += 4` stubs whose real epilogues owed 12 and 36 bytes, an indirect call landing on a stub that pops the wrong amount is exactly the expected shape, and safe_stub still reads 8 every run. State unchanged: 44 kernel calls / 5 failed icalls / 23 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, reached 101, callsites 357, deterministic.

entries.claim: CORRECTION to #79: its central negative - "recomp_esp_escape NEVER FIRED, so the over-pop is not in a direct call" - is WRONG. It did fire. My grep was truncated at 20 lines and the 40+ `[KERNEL] ... esp=` lines crowded the `[ESP]` report out of view. The first and biggest escape IS a direct call: sub_00227F90, delta +180
entries.evidence: HOW I GOT IT WRONG, recorded because the method failure matters more than the fact. To look for esp reports in the first RECOMP_CHECK_ABI run I ran `Select-String -Pattern "esp" | Where-Object { $_.Line -notmatch "^\[ABI\]" } | Select-Object -First 20`. Every one of the first 20 matches was a `[KERNEL] #N: ordinal X esp=0x00F7FFxx` progress line - there are 40+ of them and they appear early in the log. The `[ESP]` report sits after them and was cut off by `-First 20`. I then reported "ZERO esp reports" as a finding and built ledger #79's whole conclusion on it. RECOMP_ABI_CALL was not modified between the two builds, so that report was present in the first run too and I simply did not see it. This is the same class of mistake as the shared probe counter that hid the interesting site three times today: a display limit silently truncating evidence, then a confident conclusion drawn from the truncated view. Do not conclude "X never happens" from a head-limited grep - count the matches first, or grep for the exact tag. WHAT THE FULL RESULT ACTUALLY IS, from the rebuilt binary (coverage identical at distinct=101 / callsites=357, so the instrumentation remains behaviour-neutral and both runs describe the same execution), four escapes in firing order: (1) "[ESP] sub_00227F90 left esp outside the stack: 00F7FF54 -> 00F80008 (delta +180)" - NO "icall to" prefix, so this is recomp_esp_escape, a DIRECT call, and it is the FIRST transition out of range and the one to chase; (2) "[ESP] icall to sub_00220870 ... 00F7FF58 -> 00F8002C (delta +212)"; (3) "[ESP] icall to sub_00211530 ... 00F7FFF8 -> 00F80008 (delta +16)"; (4) "[ESP] icall to sub_00216F70 ... 00F80000 -> 00F80004 (delta +4)". SO BOTH PATHS OVER-POP, direct and indirect - #79's narrowing was not just unproven, it was backwards. The new RECOMP_ESP_WATCH added to RECOMP_ICALL / RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE / RECOMP_ITAIL is still worth having: it produced entries 2-4, which the direct-call check could never have caught, and it names target VAs. PRIME SUSPECT sub_00227F90: it is both the first esp escape (+180) and already present in tools_data/abi_violations.txt as "[ABI] sub_00227F90 did not restore: ebx 6769203A->45747865 esi 624F6174->6769203A" - ASCII ": ig" -> "extE" and "taOb" -> ": ig", i.e. it is moving string bytes through the callee-saved registers. A function that both destroys ebx/esi AND leaves esp 180 bytes high is a much stronger candidate than anything on the raw violation list. NOTE ON sub_00216F70, the 6-byte getter seeded in #78: its escape is only +4 and it starts from esp = 0x00F80000, i.e. esp was ALREADY at the stack ceiling when it ran. Its lifted body pops exactly 4 for its `ret`, which is correct. It is a VICTIM of the earlier drift, not a cause - do not revert it on this evidence. NEXT STEP: bracket sub_00227F90 with entry/exit esp probes and account for every push against every pop, the method that cracked #71. Tree state unchanged and verified: normal build 44 kernel calls / 5 failed icalls / 23 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, reached 101, callsites 357, deterministic 2 of 2. The recomp_types.h change is behaviour-neutral - the normal build's numbers are identical before and after it.

entries.claim: THE 180 BYTES ARE FOUND: sub_00204020 captures _icall_esp ABOVE its callee-saved pushes of esi and edi, so a FAILED ICALL rolls esp back past both saves while the epilogue pops them anyway - 8 bytes per call, in a loop, up a six-level chain. BUT the obvious fix REGRESSES the boot 101 -> 64 reached with 37 lost and ZERO gained, so it is reverted and the site carries a warning comment
entries.evidence: SIX LEVELS, EVERY ONE BRACKETED WITH PROBES RATHER THAN REASONED - and reasoning was wrong at every level, because four of the six functions balance perfectly on paper. (1) sub_00227F90, entry esp 0x00F7FF54: the five sub_00209650 calls gain instead of losing 4 each - after call 1 esp=0x00F7FF80 where 0x00F7FF50 was due (48 lost), then 32 lost on each of calls 2-5. 48 + 4x32 = 176, plus 4 for its own ret = 180, matching RECOMP_CHECK_ABI's "[ESP] sub_00227F90 ... 00F7FF54 -> 00F80008 (delta +180)" to the byte. Its own arithmetic (5 pushes, one `esp + 0x14`) is correct. (2) sub_00209650 is a callback dispatcher reading its target from MEM32(esp+8). Balanced. (3) sub_00227F50, the first callback: loc_00227F50 0x00F7FF44 -> loc_00227F55 0x00F7FF44 proves its sub_00227F90 re-entry is balanced; loc_00227F88 reads 0x00F7FF48 where 0x00F7FF18 was due. Its own 11 pushes = 0x2C are cleaned by `esp + 0x2C`. Balanced. (4) sub_002235D0 loses 24 per hit, twice on this path = 48. Walking all 60 labels: prologue correct (-0x108 frame, -0x10 for four pushes, steady at 0x00F7FDFC), then loc_00223736 -> loc_00223738 jumps +0x18 across ONE ICALL that pushes only a 4-byte dummy. DECISIVE DETAIL: the recursive INNER frame runs that same ICALL BALANCED. Probing the target explained why - "[T:PRE] #1 target=0x00226250" then POST unchanged, versus "[T:PRE] #2 target=0x00221F50 esp=0x00F7FDFC" then "[T:POST] #2 esp=0x00F7FE14". Same code, different callback. (5) sub_00221F50 is balanced at all 17 labels until its last call: loc_0022216C 0x00F7FDE0 -> loc_00222193 0x00F7FDF8 where 0x00F7FDE0 was due. Its own frame (esp-8 plus four pushes = 24, epilogue pops 4 registers plus `esp + 8` = 24) balances. (6) sub_0021ACD0 walked at 38 labels: prologue correct (-0x14 then -0xC = 32 wound, steady at 0x00F7FDAC), and loc_0021ADFB -> loc_0021AE17 gains 8 EVERY LOOP ITERATION - iteration 1 0x00F7FDAC -> 0x00F7FDB4, iteration 2 0x00F7FDB4 -> 0x00F7FDBC. Three iterations = 24. Both of ITS paths balance on paper too. THE TERMINAL CAUSE: the only call between those two labels is sub_00204020, thiscall with NO stack arguments. Its body is `{ uint32_t _icall_esp = g_esp; PUSH32(esp, esi); esi = ecx; eax = MEM32(esi); PUSH32(esp, edi); ... RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE(...); }` - _icall_esp captured ABOVE both callee-saved pushes. On failure RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE does `g_esp = saved_esp`, rolling past esi and edi; the epilogue (via sub_00204039 / sub_00204086) pops them regardless, so the caller ends 8 bytes high. Two saves = 8 bytes = exactly the per-iteration figure, and the run has 5 failed icalls. This is precisely the class tools_data/find_icall_esp_saves.py exists for; its fix comments are already present in sub_00209650 and sub_002235D0, and sub_00204020 was missed. THE SWEEP: 16,236 icall save points scanned, 3,140 capture across register saves - 2,519 at 4 bytes, 403 at 8, 143 at 12, 63 at 16, 7 at 20, 3 at 24, 2 at 28. IMPORTANT FRAMING: the skew only materialises when the ICALL actually FAILS, so these are LATENT sites, not 3,140 live bugs. THE FIX WAS APPLIED AND REVERTED. Moving the capture below the two pushes is correct in isolation and cut failed_icalls 5 -> 2 and heap_allocs 23 -> 22, but measured deterministic 2 of 2 it took reached 101 -> 64 and callsites 357 -> 265, and diff_reached.py returned "NOTHING new was reached and 37 were lost. That is a regression on this measure. Do not explain it away." Zero gained is the deciding difference from #72, which gained 4 while losing 17 and was rightly kept. Reverted; tree confirmed back at 44/5/23/8 with reached 101 and callsites 357. The site now carries a comment recording what was tried, the exact numbers, and the instruction to judge any retry on diff_reached.py rather than on failed_icalls - which improved while the boot got worse, a trap worth naming. STILL OPEN: why removing a real 8-byte skew makes the boot die earlier. Something downstream either depends on it or is masked by it. That question, not the skew, is now the wall.
